items.title: Noether normalization over the fibre: factorization through affine space with finite fibre map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism of affine schemes f: X to S and a point s with fibre dimension d, the lemma produces a factorization of f through affine space of relative dimension d over S such that the induced morphism on the fibres over s is finite (statement lines 3415-3424). The proof is a direct transcription of the situation into rings: writing S = Spec(A), X = Spec(B) and choosing a surjection onto B from a polynomial ring, Noether normalization supplies elements y_1 to y_d in the subalgebra generated by the chosen variables such that the induced A-algebra map from A[t_1,...,t_d] to B becomes finite after tensoring with the residue field at s (proof lines 3426-3437). The same elements define the required factorization and the finiteness statement is exactly the fibrewise one. The claim is H2: one algebra input applied in the relative setting, with the transcription between the geometry and the rings carried out explicitly.
